guitar.guitaristsText: Keith Richards / Ronnie Wood / Mick Taylor
guitar.modelsText: Fender Telecaster ('Micawber', 5-string open-G) / Gibson Les Paul / ES series
guitar.evidence: Keith Richards' 5-string open-G-tuned Telecaster 'Micawber' is one of the most famous specific guitars in rock history; this justifies high rather than medium confidence.
guitar.notes: Upgraded confidence from medium to high due to Richards' very specifically documented guitar/tuning setup.

tone.target: jangly edge-of-breakup Stones rhythm with slight compression
tone.profile: jangly edge-of-breakup Stones rhythm with slight compression
tone.summary: The chain uses Comp for initial punch, followed by a light OD boost (Green OD) to achieve the 'edge-of-breakup' grit. The UK 45/UK Vintage 4x12 combination provides the necessary chimey, mid-focused British sound, finished with Chorus and Room reverb.

rig.name: The Rolling Stones - Beast Of Burden - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Achieve the required 'slight compression' and punch for rhythm playing.
Provide the 'light grit' and 'edge-of-breakup' sound without heavy overdrive.
Bypass (No dedicated distortion needed due to Green OD and amp choice).
Simulate the classic British low-gain sound and chimey character.
Provide the classic British cabinet tone and clarity.
Tweak the tone to emphasize jangly highs and tighten the low end.
Add subtle movement and width to the rhythm tone.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the current IR for a more open, jangly sound that better captures the Tele/Rickenbacker chime.

proposals.reason: The current UK Vintage 4x12 is too closed and dark for the required jangly, chimey tone.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and sparkle in the high end.
